races.name: Andersons - Kitchens Beautifully Built Around You Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Runninsonofagun
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 24-day break who may have needed his last run at Ayr
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win (from 18 attempts) came back in August 2024 and he was down the field on this month's reappearance at Ayr; however, he may have needed that run and he's on a competitive mark on the pick of last season's form (including here); each-way chance if he's back on song.

runners_data.name: Lever Up
runners_data.note: Prominent racer on a reduced mark following a fair reappearance at Wetherby last month
runners_data.spotlight: Made it 0-11 when sixth of 12 on last month's reappearance at Wetherby but it wasn't a bad performance and he could improve for it; his reduced mark appeals on last season's best form and he's not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Yafaarr
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best form is on AW but showed promise when fourth at Redcar recently
runners_data.spotlight: Best form has come on AW and he made it 0-6 on turf when fourth of eight, beaten about 4l, at Redcar (7f, good) three weeks ago; however, he kept on well and his last win came over 1m at Newcastle last October; has an each-way shout up in trip.

runners_data.name: Jewel Maker
runners_data.note: 11-year-old hold-up horse who is 6lb lower than his last win but has fitness concerns
runners_data.spotlight: 11yo who has plenty to prove on the evidence of this year's three runs; however, he's 6lb lower than when winning at Redcar last October and perhaps the return to Carlisle will trigger a revival, with his course form figures reading 4106231.

runners_data.name: Pisanello
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up runner who isn't the force of old but showed promise fourth at Hamilton
runners_data.spotlight: 9yo who is winless since June 2024 and is nothing like the force of old; however, his recent 4l fourth of eight at Hamilton (8.3f, good) wasn't devoid of promise and he's another 3lb lower today; not ruled out each-way.

runners_data.name: Krissy
runners_data.note: In-form front-runner with two recent Musselburgh wins at this distance on good ground
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who has begun to tap into the abundant potential in her pedigree, with two wins at Musselburgh (1m1f, good) this spring; has also run well away from Musselburgh; did it very easily last Thursday and a 5lb penalty is unlikely to stop her if her fine form continues (she's 6lb well in).

runners_data.name: Hostility
runners_data.note: 16-race maiden who struggles to settle but kept on well over 7f at his last start
runners_data.spotlight: 16-race maiden who can be difficult to settle and was well beaten at Ripon (1m, good) last month on sole previous run beyond 7f; however, he kept on strongly for seventh of 13 at Catterick (7f, good) last time, suggesting this trip might be worth a go, and his mark continues to fall; visor removed.

runners_data.name: Condotti
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 223-day break on a career-low mark but fitness unknown
runners_data.spotlight: Ten-race maiden but he ran some good races last season and reappears on a career-low mark; can give a good account if fully tuned up.

runners_data.name: Golden Valour
runners_data.note: 10-year-old hold-up horse coming off an encouraging fifth at Ayr nine days ago
runners_data.spotlight: 10yo who posted a fairly encouraging reappearance run at Ayr (7f, good to firm) last Wednesday, when rallying for fifth of eight; each-way possibilities if building on that run now back up in trip.

races.paceDynamic: Runninsonofagun and Krissy are the confirmed front-runners who will contest the early pace in this 1m1f contest, creating an honest gallop from the start. Both have natural speed and the inclination to lead, which should ensure a true tempo throughout. Lever Up and Hostility will sit prominently behind the leaders, while the hold-up horses like Yafaarr, Jewel Maker, and Pisanello will look to come from behind. This sustained pace will favour the prominent racers who can track the leaders without burning energy early, as they'll be perfectly positioned to strike when the front-runners tire.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent racers profit
scenarios.trigger: If Runninsonofagun and Krissy duel hard early and compromise each other
scenarios.body: The honest pace will set up perfectly for horses tracking just behind the leaders who can pounce in the final furlong. Lever Up and Condotti are ideally positioned to benefit from this tactical scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runner dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Krissy gets an uncontested lead and controls the tempo
scenarios.body: Her recent Musselburgh victories show she's in career-best form and can dictate terms over this ideal distance. Runninsonofagun will struggle to match her current level of improvement.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and burns out the leaders
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will play into the hands of those held up, particularly on this fair track that rewards patient tactics. Yafaarr and Pisanello have the finishing kick to capitalise on a fast-run race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shock maiden breakthrough
scenarios.trigger: If Hostility finally settles properly and gets the strong pace he needs
scenarios.body: His tendency to be keen has undermined him previously, but this trip could suit better if he relaxes. The honest tempo would perfectly suit his late-running style if connections have sorted his settling issues.

watchPoints.text: Krissy could get an uncontested lead if Runninsonofagun doesn't fire fresh from his break
Condotti's fitness after 223 days off despite being on an attractive career-low mark
Hostility's settling ability over this longer trip as he's been keen in shorter races
The pace strength if both front-runners cooperate rather than contest early
Golden Valour's improvement from his Ayr run given the short turnaround

races.name: Grandad Bill Whinnow EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Lincoln Warrior
runners_data.note: Unknown quantity as a Saxon Warrior half-brother with solid pedigree, but debut runners face tactical disadvantage in small field sprint
runners_data.spotlight: 28,000euros yearling; fifth foal; Saxon Warrior half-brother to winners Alpheratz (1m; RPR 99) and Immutable (1m-1m4f Flat including 2yo, 98); dam unraced half-sister to St Leger runner-up Arrest and French Derby third Detain; market check advised on debut but it's possible he's best watched.

runners_data.name: Justice Time
runners_data.note: Another newcomer with speed-oriented female family including Listed winner Orlaith, trainer's yard out of form recently
runners_data.spotlight: 10,000euros yearling; third foal; dam once-raced half-sister to winners Orlaith (5f 2yo Listed), Florida Filly (5f 2yo) and Tammy Wynette (5f); it's likely this Inns Of Court newcomer will improve for the run.

runners_data.name: Aodhan
runners_data.spotlight: 18,000gns yearling; seventh foal; Caturra half-brother to winners Lady Roxby (5f including 2yo; RPR 89) and Lezardrieux (prolific 5f/6f including 2yo; 85); dam 5f 2yo winner (75); trainer/owner have a very promising 2yo on their hands in Adonius; the betting could be informative on debut.

runners_data.name: State Of Gold
runners_data.note: Prominent early but fades badly in finish, poor debut at Redcar despite market support suggests limited ability
runners_data.spotlight: Sent off just 9-2 for last month's debut at Redcar (5f, good to firm) but finished down the field; upset in stalls and withdrawn at Musselburgh nine days later (25-1 at the time); others make greater appeal.

runners_data.name: Tamam Star
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who ran well on debut before disappointing second start, needs clear passage which may be easier in small field
runners_data.spotlight: Promising fourth on debut at Musselburgh (5f, good) last month, when he would have gone close with a clear passage; took a backwards step at Thirsk (5f, good to firm) six days later but it's possible that run came too soon; key player if leaving last time behind.

runners_data.name: Call Nicki
runners_data.note: Natural front runner with improved recent form, likely to get easy lead which suits her style perfectly
runners_data.spotlight: Improved upon her debut run at Thirsk (5f, good to firm) on May 2 when third there (5f, good) a fortnight ago, having attracted some market support; she's a leading player on the back of that latest effort.

runners_data.name: Brixworth Bandit
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who showed pace on debut before fading, trainer struggling for winners but improvement possible
runners_data.spotlight: Showed pace and had a wide trip when well-beaten seventh of nine on this month's debut at Beverley (5f, good to soft); improvement is possible but he needs to take a sizeable step forward if he's to threaten today.

runners_data.name: May Bee In Profit
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid recent form including close second, 6f experience last time may help her late stamina
runners_data.spotlight: Close second at Beverley (5f, good to soft) on second start and third at Windsor (6f, good) last time, when shaping as though she would benefit from this return to 5f; every chance she'll be bang there.

races.paceDynamic: Call Nicki will dictate terms from the front with no other confirmed front runners in this small field. Tamam Star and State Of Gold are likely to track her prominently early, but State Of Gold has shown a tendency to fade late. May Bee In Profit typically races prominently but may settle slightly off the pace given her recent 6f experience. This should create an honest but not frantic gallop over the minimum trip. **This race shape clearly favours prominent racers and on-pace horses who can travel close to Call Nicki without being outpaced by her early speed.**

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Call Nicki Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Call Nicki gets an uncontested lead and dictates a steady early pace...
scenarios.body: She can save enough for a strong finish having avoided early pressure, making full use of her front-running style. Her recent third at Thirsk showed improved form and the tactics suit perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Develops
scenarios.trigger: If Tamam Star or May Bee In Profit press Call Nicki early and create genuine pace...
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will expose stamina limitations and favour horses with the best finishing kick from close range. May Bee In Profit's recent 6f experience could prove crucial for her late surge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If Call Nicki goes too slow early and the field bunches up behind her...
scenarios.body: A sprint finish from the final furlong will emerge, suiting any horse with natural speed regardless of early position. The lightly-raced newcomers could benefit from the reduced emphasis on tactical positioning.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Early Pace Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses challenge Call Nicki's lead from the start creating strong early fractions...
scenarios.body: The pace will set up perfectly for any hold-up horse or late closer to sweep past tired leaders. Brixworth Bandit showed early pace on debut and might benefit from a truly-run race.

watchPoints.text: Call Nicki's early fractions will determine the entire race shape - if she goes too fast early she becomes vulnerable to closers
State Of Gold's stalls behaviour after being upset before withdrawal at Musselburgh could disrupt the start
Tamam Star's position early will reveal whether jockey plans to press Call Nicki or sit behind and wait
Both newcomers Lincoln Warrior and Justice Time represent unknown quantities with Brian Ellison's yard badly out of form
May Bee In Profit's settling position will indicate whether connections think she needs the 6f experience to stretch out or sprint speed to win

races.name: Andersons - Quality For The Home Handicap

runners_data.name: Get Up Everybody
runners_data.note: Prominent style perfectly suited to track the expected strong early pace and David Nolan's 3rd at Pontefract shows current form
runners_data.spotlight: 0-11 but has frequently run well, finishing third Pontefract (5f, good to soft) last month before a very close fourth at Redcar (6f, good); perhaps the first-time cheekpieces will eke out something extra; in the mix.

runners_data.name: Midnight Lir
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces tactical difficulties in a likely strong-run race after 26 days off
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten 19 times since his last win in September 2023 and good runs have been scarce over the last year and a bit; however, it's possible he'll improve for this month's reappearance outing and he's not discounted off a handy mark in a reapplied tongue-tie and first-time blinkers.

runners_data.name: Pop Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose reduced mark appeals but recent poor form and 33-day break are concerns
runners_data.spotlight: His reduced mark appeals on form as recent as last September but he's struggled to get competitive on his seven runs since December.

runners_data.name: Dandy Dinmont
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with winning form at Beverley but inconsistency remains a worry despite only 2lb rise
runners_data.spotlight: He's inconsistent but he was back on song when winning at Beverley (5f, good to firm) this month; he's just 2lb higher today and is a leading player if backing up that latest performance.

runners_data.name: Lindoro
runners_data.note: Natural leader returning to turf after poor AW run but dam's 5f winning background suggests trip suits
runners_data.spotlight: Soundly beaten on sole run this season (6f, AW) but showed promise last summer on his other two starts (6f/7f, good/good to soft); his dam was a useful 5f winner and he could appreciate the drop in trip on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Komorkis
runners_data.note: Hold-up style may struggle to get competitive position but 4th at Nottingham shows ability off this mark
runners_data.spotlight: Won a three-runner novice at Musselburgh (5f, good to soft) last September and very close fourth in a handicap at Nottingham (5f, good) last month on her seasonal/stable debut; below-par in a first-time hood (now left off) at Nottingham (5f, good) three weeks ago but she's not written off.

runners_data.name: Digital
runners_data.note: Front-runner who won off this mark in February but poor recent turf form suggests he needs major improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time turf winner who won off today's mark at Newcastle (5f, AW) in February; however, he's finished down the field on his last four starts and a major turnaround is necessary.

runners_data.name: Albegone
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with recent placed form but needs to reverse recent disappointments to feature
runners_data.spotlight: Close second at Newcastle (5f, AW) in February and likewise at Nottingham (5f, good) last month; however, soundly beaten on his three starts since and he needs to raise his game.

runners_data.name: Wee Mary
runners_data.note: Hold-up style benefits from 13lb weight allowance and recent consistent efforts at this level
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win (from 23 attempts) came in AW classified in January; however, she's run well off this mark in turf handicaps on her last four starts (5f/6f, good/good to firm) and there's every chance she'll be bang there.

runners_data.name: Ski Angel
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits the likely pace scenario though form dipped last time at Hamilton
runners_data.spotlight: Not at the top of her game at Hamilton (5f, good) a fortnight ago but before that she was an encouraging fourth on her comeback at Ayr (5f, good to firm); third in this last year and might not be far away if bouncing back.

races.paceDynamic: Lindoro and Digital are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead in this 5f sprint. With both horses likely to go forward aggressively from the gates, they'll create an honest gallop that should suit horses positioned prominently or those with tactical pace. The strong early pace will stretch the field and put pressure on hold-up horses like Midnight Lir, Pop Star, and Komorkis to find racing room in the closing stages. This race shape clearly favours prominent racers and those with tactical speed who can track the leaders without getting involved in the early battle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Early Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Lindoro and Digital both break smartly and dispute the lead through the first two furlongs
scenarios.body: The honest gallop will suit horses like Get Up Everybody and Ski Angel who can sit prominent without leading, allowing them to pick up the pieces when the leaders tire. The strong pace will set up perfectly for prominent racers with finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders settles and allows the other to dictate a steadier tempo
scenarios.body: Digital or Lindoro could steal a march by controlling the pace, making it harder for hold-up horses to make ground. The tactical scenario would favour the controlling leader and any prominent racer who tracks them closely.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is truly fierce and both leaders empty out dramatically in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The collapse of the front-runners would create opportunities for closers like Komorkis and Midnight Lir to sweep past tired leaders. However, this requires perfect timing and racing room that may not materialise in a competitive 5f sprint.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Digital or Lindoro gets an uncontested lead while the other fails to go forward as expected
scenarios.body: The lone leader could pinch crucial lengths and prove hard to peg back over the minimum trip. This scenario particularly suits whichever front-runner faces less early pressure and can dictate their own fractions.

watchPoints.text: Digital's willingness to lead early after four consecutive poor runs - if he's reluctant to go forward the pace dynamic changes completely
Lindoro's turf form transfer from last season given his sole 2024 run was a poor AW effort over 6f
Get Up Everybody's ability to settle prominently with David Nolan rather than getting involved in the early speed battle
Racing room for hold-up horses Komorkis and Midnight Lir in what could become a cavalry charge finish
Dandy Dinmont's consistency given his Jekyll and Hyde form pattern despite recent Beverley success

races.name: Andersons - Proudly Local Since 1888 Handicap

runners_data.name: Only Dream Big
runners_data.note: Improved hold-up performer with good recent Redcar form, suited by the likely soft pace but may need luck from the back
runners_data.spotlight: Improved upon her four 2yo runs when close fourth in handicap at Redcar (7f, good) on recent reappearance, when a stumble didn't help; firmly in calculations on the back of that effort.

runners_data.name: Ghadra
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with fading tendencies, basement mark offers hope but 64 days off and poor recent form are concerning
runners_data.spotlight: She has a useful pedigree (raced once for Al Shaqab) and she has a basement opening mark; however, she has shown very little and a transformation is needed in a first-time visor.

runners_data.name: Kode Grey
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner faces no pace pressure, recent Ripon third shows he's in good form off this same handicap mark
runners_data.spotlight: Showed improved form and good pace when third on handicap debut at Ripon (6f, good) 12 days ago; on the shortlist today off the same mark.

runners_data.name: Saxon Grace
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with fading issues, two stable runs showed promise but needs to prove 6f is optimal trip
runners_data.spotlight: 0-9 but her two runs for this stable haven't been without promise (6f/7f, AW) and 6f may prove to be her best trip; each-way possibilities.

runners_data.name: Ganthorpe
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse better than recent Redcar seventh suggests, earlier form shows he can be competitive at this level
runners_data.spotlight: Made it 0-9 when 4l seventh of 14 to Auspicious at Redcar (6f, good) three weeks ago; however, he's better than that, as evidenced by some positive runs earlier this year, and he has an each-way squeak if bouncing back.

runners_data.name: What A Tahoo
runners_data.note: Improving hold-up filly whose Ripon third was career-best, quick return and good form trend are positive signs
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7 but she ran her best race yet when third at Ripon (6f, good) 12 days ago; could be in the shake-up if confirming that promise.

runners_data.name: Saxon Gem
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from basement mark making handicap debut, triple-figure odds previously suggest limited ability
runners_data.spotlight: Triple-figure odds for all three starts (6f, good to firm/good) and hasn't achieved much; however, she now goes handicapping off a basement mark and she's from a family her trainer has done well with; could go well.

runners_data.name: Muddy Nora
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with poor recent form, 41 days off and well beaten at Nottingham last time out
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten at big odds on her three 2yo starts and down the field at 22-1 on last month's handicap and seasonal debut at Nottingham (5f, good); improvement is necessary.

runners_data.name: Auspicious
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning to form with Redcar win, proven at this level but faces 3lb penalty for recent success
runners_data.spotlight: Mixed form since she won on nursery debut at Newcastle (6f, AW) last September but she returned to winning ways at Redcar (6f, good) three weeks ago; just 3lb higher today and holds strong claims for in-form yard.

runners_data.name: Independent Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with fading tendencies, never competitive in five handicap attempts and hard to recommend
runners_data.spotlight: She's raced eight times and is yet to go off shorter than 66-1; unable to get competitive in any of her five handicaps; hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Kode Grey will make the running unopposed from the front, with all other nine runners adopting hold-up tactics further back. This creates a very soft, uncontested early pace that will build gradually through the middle stages. The large pack of hold-up horses will create a cavalry charge in the final two furlongs as they all try to close the gap simultaneously. This race shape strongly favours early leaders and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems that the massed hold-up brigade will encounter.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kode Grey Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Kode Grey gets uncontested fractions and kicks clear approaching the final furlong
scenarios.body: The lone leader dictates ideal splits and has enough in reserve to repel late challengers who leave their runs too late. The soft pace suits his front-running style perfectly against this field of hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Benefits Best
scenarios.trigger: If the large pack of hold-up horses creates significant interference in the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: The horses with the clearest runs and strongest finishing kicks prevail as several others get stopped or hampered. Class tells when the traffic clears.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sustained Kick Wins Out
scenarios.trigger: If one hold-up horse gets a dream run and produces a sustained drive from the back
scenarios.body: A horse with superior finishing speed finds clear water and powers past the tiring leader in the final 100 yards. The soft pace allows for devastating late charges.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Kode Grey goes too slowly and the field bunches up turning for home
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy sprint from two furlongs out with multiple horses in contention. Tactical speed and position become crucial in a scramble finish.

watchPoints.text: Kode Grey faces no pace pressure whatsoever with nine hold-up horses behind him, creating ideal front-running conditions
Traffic problems are almost inevitable with nine hold-up horses converging simultaneously in the final two furlongs
What A Tahoo and Only Dream Big both showed career-best efforts recently and could benefit from the likely soft pace scenario
Auspicious carries a 3lb penalty for his recent Redcar win but has proven form at this level on similar going
Saxon Grace and Saxon Gem are both making stable switches and could show improvement in new environments

races.name: andersonslimited.co.uk Handicap

runners_data.name: Taylormade Lad
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 26-day break with course and distance win under his belt plus Connor Beasley's valuable 5lb claim.
runners_data.spotlight: Won over C&D (good to firm) last August and this lightly raced 4yo reappeared with a respectable third at Hamilton (1m3f, good) this month behind comfortable winner Alpine Sierra, who followed up; he's 11lb better off with his old rival this afternoon and could build on that latest effort.

runners_data.name: Alpine Sierra
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner in red-hot form with back-to-back wins using these exact tactics, Lauren Young takes off 5lb.
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Hamilton (1m3f, good) on May 3 and again had plenty in hand when following up at Musselburgh (1m4f, good) last week, when switched to front-running tactics; this thriving 8yo has strong claims under 4lb penalty.

runners_data.name: Naturalia
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who needs strong pace to aim at, 3lb lower than her good second at Catterick but struggled over shorter recently.
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't threatened over 1m1f on her last two starts but before those she reappeared with a good second at Catterick (1m4f, good) and is 3lb lower today; has won here and could have a big part to play back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Ravenscraig Castle
runners_data.note: Hold-up handicapper returning to Flat after 78-day break, on handy mark based on last year's best form but rusty.
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off over hurdles last time but ran well in that code in March; he's on a handy mark on last year's best Flat form; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Sweet Kiss
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who won three times last season but may have needed her comeback run 12 days ago, Jake Dickson's 7lb claim helps.
runners_data.spotlight: She won three times under Jake Dickson last August/September (1m2f, good to firm-good to soft) and may have needed her comeback run at Hamilton (1m3f, good) 12 days ago; however, she was well beaten and a swift and major turnaround is necessary.

runners_data.name: Himself
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse dropping back from 2m after AW winning streak, 18 days since last run may leave him short of peak fitness.
runners_data.spotlight: Won three in a row over 1m6f on AW early this year; he was returning from a three-month break when weakening over 2m at Catterick this month and drops back down in trip today, but he has to prove he's fully effective on turf.

runners_data.name: Fallons First
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare returning from 316-day absence, hard to fancy despite Jack Nicholls' 5lb claim after such a long layoff.
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off when upped to 1m2f at Leicester last July and absent since; however, prior to that she kept on well for fourth on her handicap debut at Wetherby (1m, good to firm) and this very lightly raced 4yo remains one to be interested in for her top yard at this sort of trip.

races.paceDynamic: Alpine Sierra has switched to front-running tactics and won her last two races in that style, while Taylormade Lad will sit prominent having shown gate speed previously. With only these two likely to be forward early in this small field, Alpine Sierra can dictate terms without serious pressure through the early stages. The majority of the field - Naturalia, Sweet Kiss, Himself, Ravenscraig Castle and Fallons First - all prefer to be held up, creating a bunched finish behind a controlled pace. This race shape strongly favours the early leaders who can control the tempo and kick clear before the hold-up horses can organize their challenges.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alpine Sierra Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Alpine Sierra leads unchallenged and maintains her recent front-running form.
scenarios.body: She can dictate a steady pace that suits her stamina before kicking clear in the straight, making it difficult for the hold-up horses to peg her back. Her recent victories using these exact tactics give her a clear edge in this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too slow and allows the back markers to time their runs perfectly.
scenarios.body: The prominent horses may go too steady early, allowing Naturalia or Sweet Kiss to unleash devastating late kicks. Their class and turn of foot could prove decisive if they get the right racing room in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Taylormade Lad Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Taylormade Lad can press Alpine Sierra early and wear her down.
scenarios.body: His course and distance win combined with freshness after a break could see him outlast the front-runner in a battle. Connor Beasley's claiming allowance provides a useful weight advantage in a tight finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the favourites fail to handle the tactical nature and an outsider finds clear running.
scenarios.body: Himself drops back to a more suitable trip after his AW wins, while Ravenscraig Castle returns to the Flat on a handy mark. Both could benefit if the pace collapses and creates a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Alpine Sierra's early position - if she gets an uncontested lead she becomes very hard to peg back given her recent front-running dominance.
Sweet Kiss's jumping from the stalls - she needs to break smartly to get cover in this small field or risk being caught wide.
Taylormade Lad's fitness after 26 days off - any signs of rustiness early could compromise his prominent racing style.
Naturalia's settling - if she pulls hard early it will compromise her finishing kick from her preferred hold-up position.
The pace through the first half-mile - too slow will favour the closers while too fast will play into Alpine Sierra's stamina strengths.

races.name: Hoover - Performance That Lasts Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: Singoura
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare whose turf record is concerning despite recent placed efforts showing promise
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7 on turf but only beaten just over a length in her last two starts, the latest when second of eight at Redcar (7f, good) this month; that form is working out well and respected off 1lb higher.

runners_data.name: Finn Ironside
runners_data.note: Prominent runner drawn widest but Tom Eaves can overcome the draw, 1lb below last winning mark
runners_data.spotlight: Still 1lb below his last winning mark and ran well when third of 16 at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) last month (a nose ahead of Singoura); drawn widest, but still high on list.

runners_data.name: Glorious Kitty
runners_data.note: Front-running type who broke maiden nine days ago and drops in trip, 4lb well in with claim
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at the 15th attempt when making all under Lewis Chalkley in an Ayr apprentice handicap (1m, good to firm) nine days ago; 4lb well in and dropping in trip shouldn't be a problem, but whether she will be allowed her own way again is debatable.

runners_data.name: Sir David
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with sole course and distance win but regressive form since returning to action
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success came over C&D from 4lb higher last August when trained by Stella Barclay, but regressive in the meantime including in three starts since returning for this yard last month; best watched.

runners_data.name: Valentine Catcher
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner better at shorter trips with 15-race losing streak despite being well handicapped
runners_data.spotlight: Still 3lb lower than when second of eight at Pontefract (6f, good) last month, but losing run up to 15 and he does seem best at shorter.

runners_data.name: King Sharja
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who was just denied eight days ago and runs 2lb well in off recent near-miss
runners_data.spotlight: 2lb well in having only just been denied at Southwell (7f, AW) eight days ago and 1lb lower than when successful at Beverley (7f, good to firm) last July; respected.

runners_data.name: No Nay Nevermind
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning after 62 days off with concerning 0-18 record despite placed efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Twice runner-up off a higher mark at Newcastle (7f, AW) late last year, but now 0-18; others make greater appeal.

runners_data.name: Pallas Lord
runners_data.note: Natural front runner with perfect 1-1 course record and good recent third at Hamilton over further
runners_data.spotlight: Handy sort who is 1-1 here and ran well returned to turf when beaten a short head and a neck into third of eight at Hamilton (1m, good) a fortnight ago; ground faster than good probably not ideal, though.

runners_data.name: Rory's Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making stable debut after 11 months off, best efforts came on all-weather surfaces
runners_data.spotlight: Placed once in six starts for Paul Attwater with his best efforts coming on the AW; picked up for 1,000gns in March and drops in trip on stable debut after 11 months off; market informative.

runners_data.name: She's A Goldigger
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with 0-13 record who prefers softer ground conditions than today's good going
runners_data.spotlight: 0-13 and best efforts have come on ground on the soft side of good; hard to recommend from out of the weights.

races.paceDynamic: Pallas Lord will lead unopposed from the start, with Finn Ironside and Glorious Kitty settling prominently behind him in the early stages. The lack of genuine pace pressure means Pallas Lord can dictate fractions and kick clear turning for home, while the prominent runners get first run on the field. With a moderate gallop likely and the leaders not being pressured early, this race shape strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can position close to the pace from the outset.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Pallas Lord gets soft fractions and isn't challenged early
scenarios.body: The 8-year-old veteran dictates throughout and has enough left to hold off late challengers, benefiting from his 1-1 course record. His tactical speed and Jason Hart's experience prove decisive in a race lacking genuine early pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Finn Ironside or Glorious Kitty get perfect trips behind the leader
scenarios.body: The eventual winner shadows Pallas Lord before striking in the final furlong when the leader begins to tire. Tom Eaves on Finn Ironside or the in-form Glorious Kitty capitalize on their forward positions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The moderate early gallop sets up a dash from the back, allowing a closer with tactical speed to sweep up. King Sharja's recent near-miss form or Valentine Catcher's class could prove telling in a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the favourites fail to fire and pace falls apart
scenarios.body: A lightly-weighted runner like She's A Goldigger or the returning Rory's Gold finds improvement from a handy position. The chaotic finish allows an unexpected winner to emerge from the pack.

watchPoints.text: Pallas Lord gets uncontested lead and Jason Hart can dictate suicidal fractions for the field
Finn Ironside overcomes widest draw as Tom Eaves may need to use horse early to get position
Glorious Kitty handles drop back to seven furlongs after recent mile success with apprentice claim
King Sharja reproduces recent Southwell form on turf having shown best efforts on all-weather lately
Valentine Catcher settles kindly despite hold-up style in what could become messy tactical affair

races.name: Hoover - Performance That Lasts Handicap (Div II)

runners_data.name: Kings Merchant
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been well-beaten recently despite a tumbling mark and faces a tactical disadvantage in a race with many similar profiles
runners_data.spotlight: Won four times in 2024, but losing run up to 14 despite a tumbling mark; fair effort when fourth of 13 at Catterick (7f, good) 18 days ago, though, and the winner has gone in again since; each way claims.

runners_data.name: Carolus Magnus
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who should get an easy lead after a 30-day break, though lack of early pressure could see him caught late by stronger finishers
runners_data.spotlight: Not the most prolific, but he was returning from 134 days off when beaten just a neck at Musselburgh (7f, good) last month; respected off 1lb higher if coming on from that.

runners_data.name: The Gay Blade
runners_data.note: Prominent type who bled last time out which raises immediate fitness concerns despite showing good recent AW form
runners_data.spotlight: Handy sort who has been successful three times on the AW this year; has won four times on turf, but was found to have bled at Ayr last time; others more convincing.

runners_data.name: Jamaican Storm
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best form has been on AW surfaces and faces a difficult tactical position with many similar runners
runners_data.spotlight: 1-19 and his best form has come on the AW, albeit he didn't run very well at Southwell last time and his previous fourth of 13 at Thirsk (1m, good) was better; frame material again based on that effort.

runners_data.name: Jet Warrior
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong recent form including a decisive win just nine days ago, but faces potential traffic problems from wide draw
runners_data.comment: Came good with easy Ayr win last week and well treated under a penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed 4yo who has improved since handicapping and won with plenty in hand at Ayr (6f, good to firm) nine days ago; return to this trip is no problem and he's high on the list if turning out again after his even-money win in the 4.10 at Ripon (6f, good) on Thursday.

runners_data.name: Emerald Army
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who was narrowly beaten last time and sits 5lb below his last winning mark but needs luck from his patient tactics
runners_data.spotlight: Still 5lb below his last winning mark and was having only his third start for the yard when beaten a neck by a much better-fancied stablemate at Catterick (7f, good) eight days ago; already due a 2lb rise for that and no surprise if he steps up again; major player.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from a 35-day break after a heavy defeat on turf, with question marks over his effectiveness on this surface
runners_data.spotlight: Made a successful handicap debut at Newcastle (7f, AW) last September, but there was a heavy defeat on his return to turf at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) five weeks ago.

runners_data.name: El Pinto
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has regressed since his 2-year-old form and looks outclassed in this company despite suitable tactics
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7; showed plenty of ability in both starts on soft ground as a 2yo, but has regressed in an abbreviated career since; best watched.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who was well-beaten by Jet Warrior recently and unlikely to reverse form on just a 5lb swing
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten around 4l by Jet Warrior when second of ten at Ayr (6f, good to firm) nine days ago and a 5lb pull is probably nowhere near enough; only win in 31 starts came in a 0-50 classified event.

races.paceDynamic: Carolus Magnus looks the sole confirmed front-runner and should get an uncontested lead with The Gay Blade and El Pinto providing some early company before settling. The pace will be sustainable rather than fierce, with most of the field (Kings Merchant, Jamaican Storm, Jet Warrior, Emerald Army, Ziggy's Angel, Doon The Glen) sitting off the pace in hold-up positions. This creates a tactical race where the leaders can dictate terms without pressure, but the bunched field behind will need luck in running. The race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those with early pace who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems that the large hold-up contingent will create.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leaders Dominate Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Carolus Magnus and The Gay Blade can establish early positions without interference from the main field.
scenarios.body: The sustainable pace allows the early leaders to maintain their advantage while the hold-up horses get caught in traffic behind the large field. Those who race handy avoid the scramble and have clear runs to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Find Gaps
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely strong early or the leaders falter in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The patient tactics pay off as gaps appear late, allowing the better-handicapped hold-up horses to utilise their superior finishing kicks. Class tells in the final 100 yards despite the tactical disadvantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Benefits Few
scenarios.trigger: If the large hold-up contingent creates significant interference turning for home.
scenarios.body: Multiple horses get hampered in the straight, creating a messy finish where only those with clear runs can show their true ability. The race becomes more about luck than class or tactics.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Carolus Magnus goes too slowly early and gets swamped by the field with superior finishing speed.
scenarios.body: The lacklustre gallop plays into the hands of the strongest finishers who can overcome their poor tactical positions. Superior class overcomes the moderate early pace.

watchPoints.text: Jet Warrior may struggle to get a clear run from his wide draw with so many hold-up horses likely to be tracking across
The Gay Blade's bleeding issue last time could impact his performance despite the tactical advantage of racing prominently
Carolus Magnus could get an uncontested lead but watch for signs of rust after his 30-day layoff
Traffic problems are highly likely in the straight with six hold-up horses needing to find racing room simultaneously
Emerald Army's recent neck defeat suggests he's ready to strike but his hold-up style makes him vulnerable to pace scenarios
